\caption{The GFMC charge form factor stays within $1.9\sigma$ of the reference radius at every coupling, for $\lambda=1$.
The fits use $F_1(q^2)/F_1(0)=[1+q^2\langle r^2\rangle/(6p)]^{-p}$, Eq.~\eqref{eq:app:gendip}, with $F_1$ from
$\langle J_{V^0}\rangle$ and the Lanczos method (App.~\ref{app:gfmc:lanczos}). Radii are in units of $m_\psi^{-2}$.
Uncertainties are statistical, from a bootstrap that refits every resample, and $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}$ uses the bootstrap
covariance of the $q$ points. $\langle r^2\rangle_z$ is the same radius from a three-term $z$-expansion
(App.~\ref{app:gfmc:ansatz}). The reference values come from the closed form (Coulomb meson) and the variational solution
(baryon), and $p_{\rm ref}$ is the fit of Eq.~\eqref{eq:app:gendip} to the reference $F_1$ with the radius held fixed.
The same profile sets every channel (Sec.~\ref{app:gfmc:me2ff}): $F_{V^i}=(q^i/2M_\Psi)F_1$ and
$\langle J_{T^{0i}}\rangle=(q^i/2m_\psi)F_1$ exactly, the scalar $F_S=F_1-(\langle K\rangle/2m_\psi)g(q^2)$, and the
spin-dependent form factors carry the same $q^2$ shape with group-theory normalizations.}
